title: Request fingerprinting trace stitcher and deterministic span tagging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight request fingerprinting layer and trace-stitching shim inside our SDK middleware to reliably correlate spans when upstream trace IDs are lost (retries, proxy rewrites, legacy clients). Produce deterministic low-cardinality span tags to improve dashboard aggregation and reduce noise in latency/error dashboards.
design_notes: Fingerprint algorithm: canonicalize path (template extraction when available), sort and filter query params, remove auth tokens, then compute xxhash64 + per-team salt. Produce 64-bit hex fingerprint in header X-RW-FP.

Trace stitcher: accept incoming traces with either traceparent or X-RW-FP. If traceparent missing but X-RW-FP present, look up recent in-process span cache (TTL 30s) and attach / stitch child spans to closest parent. Fall back to starting a new root span if no match.

Deterministic tags: emit route.template and op.bucket (pre-defined coarse buckets) to avoid high-cardinality model IDs or user IDs. Use configurable bucketing rules; default to 50 buckets for heavy-cardinality fields.
Sampling hints: include X-RW-SAMPLE-HINT with values {force, prefer, none} to let downstream beacons influence sampling decisions without overriding global sampler.

Performance trade-offs: keep inlined hashing code small and dependency-free for Node/Python SDKs; provide optional native extension for Go/low-latency hosts. Aim for <0.05% increase in p99 request latency.
Compatibility: header names are prefixed with X-RW- to avoid collisions; legacy clients can opt-in by setting X-RW-FP themselves once provided guidance.
Security: fingerprint excludes PII and user tokens; salt per-tenant to prevent cross-tenant correlation; policy documented for SOC2 review.
tasks: Implement canonicalizer + xxhash64 helper in node/python/go SDKs
Add middleware to attach X-RW-FP and X-RW-SAMPLE-HINT in outbound requests
Implement in-process recent-span cache with TTL and bounded size for stitch lookups
Server-side stitching adapter to accept incoming X-RW-FP and attach to ingestion pipeline
E2E tests for retry+proxy scenarios, websocket handshake coverage
Dashboard: latency/error dashboards add stitched vs unstitched breakdown and cardinality impact
Docs: SDK integration guide + security FAQ + rollout checklist
Rollout canary: enable default off for hosted customers; opt-in for Dedicated during cycle
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover canonicalization edge cases (query ordering, special chars, body-less POSTs)
Integration test: 95% of retry scenarios with dropped traceparent are successfully stitched in CI harness
Telemetry: stitch_miss_rate <= 5% on canary traffic and stable under load
Performance: adding middleware increases p99 end-to-end latency by <0.05% on supported runtimes
Cardinality: route.template + op.bucket reduce high-cardinality tag explosion by at least 80% on sample workload
Docs and security review completed and linked in ticket before broad rollout
comments: 2025-03-05 Aisha Patel: Triage - identified repeat incidents where retries from edge proxies lost traceparent. Proposal: fingerprint-based stitcher. Assigned to Marco.
2025-03-06 Marco Liu: Spike implemented prototype for Node SDK; xxhash64 chosen for speed and availability. Measured ~120ns/hash on local benchmark.
2025-03-07 Leila Ramos (PM): Reviewed design. Requested explicit defaults for bucketing rules and a clear migration path for customers that rely on URL tags.
2025-03-08 Security review (Jin Park): Confirmed PII exclusion acceptable. Request: add per-tenant salt and document storage retention for recent-span cache.
2025-03-09 Marco Liu: PR opened for Node SDK middleware (see links). Added canary-by-header rollout plan to avoid global impact.

2025-03-10 Alex Gomez (SRE): Load testing on staging shows stitch_miss_rate 2.7% at 10k rps with synthetic proxies. Noted small increase in GC for Node due to cache; recommending bounded cache size 10k entries.
blockers: Decision required: default value for X-RW-SAMPLE-HINT when client doesn't supply preference
Platform task: ingestion side needs lightweight lookup path for FP -> trace id mapping (ENG-42000)
SDK maintainers need sign-off for adding xxhash dependency in Python wheel
review_feedback: Leila Ramos: prefer explicit opt-in for Hosted customers during initial rollout
Jin Park: require automated test verifying PII is not included in fingerprint inputs
SRE (Alex): add circuit-breaker to recent-span cache to avoid memory spikes under bursts
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature flag ON for internal services + canary customers (2 weeks). Stage 2: open to Dedicated customers with opt-in toggle. Stage 3: enable-by-default for new accounts after 6 weeks and monitoring thresholds met.
notes: Avoid attaching raw URLs or user identifiers as span tags. Keep fingerprint TTL conservative (30s) to balance stitch coverage vs memory.
